classification.text_en: The raven (ghurab) is a bird God sent to the one who had killed his brother.

origin.note_en: The Quran does not describe the origin of the raven.

purpose.text_en: God sent it to show him how to cover his brother's body.

nature.text_en: The raven is described searching in the earth.

abilities.text_en: It was the means by which the man was shown how to cover his brother's body.

limitations.note_en: The Quran does not describe limits of the raven.

relationship_with_humans.text_en: The man said, woe to me, am I unable to be like this raven and cover my brother's body? He became one of those who regret.

quranic_events.text_en: After the killing of one of the two sons of Adam by the other, God sent a raven searching in the earth, and the killer was shown how to cover his brother's body.

chronological_position.note_en: The Quran gives no date for the event.

location.text_en: The raven was searching in the earth.

misconceptions.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): the verse gives the raven's role in one sentence. This profile adds nothing about what the bird did to the ground beyond 'searching in the earth'.

lessons.text_en: Educational interpretation (not scripture): a man learns from a bird how to do what he could not work out, and regret follows, which is read as a lesson in humility and in regret after wrongdoing.

vocabulary.text_en: Words used: ghurab (a raven), yabhathu fi al-ard (searching in the earth), yuwari (to cover), saw'ah (his brother's body, as covered).
